EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical development of the past 24 hours is Iran's appointment of Mohsen Rezaei as Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) and representative of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, signaling a hardline shift amid escalating tensions. Concurrently, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu formally rejected the US-backed 15-point Gaza peace plan, vowing no withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed, further complicating regional peace efforts.

IRAN
Mohsen Rezaei, former IRGC commander and military advisor to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, has been appointed as the new Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) and the Leader's representative to the council. This appointment follows President Masoud Pezeshkian's meeting with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, reportedly to discuss economic management and military developments. Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi stated that Iran is not negotiating with the US and will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the US stops breaching previously agreed Memoranda of Understanding and meets Iran's conditions. These conditions, articulated by former SNSC Secretary Mohammad Baqer Zolqadr, include an end to US threats, an end to war against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Gaza, Yemen, and Iraq, lifting the naval blockade, withdrawal of US military forces, full war reparations, lifting all sanctions, and unfreezing assets. The IRGC echoed this stance, stating the Strait will not reopen without US acceptance of all Iranian conditions. Press TV reported that Iran's parliamentary commission approved a strategic plan for Strait of Hormuz security. Oil prices rose by 1.2% following Iran's announcement of these demands and non-negotiation with the US. US President Trump, however, claimed to be "semi-negotiating" and "low keying it" with Iran, banking on economic pressure due to "massive inflation" and a lack of funds to achieve an outcome, though Axios reported he considered declaring "victory" without a nuclear deal if the Strait of Hormuz reopened. The New York Times reported that the US war on Iran has depleted American weapons stockpiles, emboldening rivals. Rosatom announced plans to increase Russian specialists at the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant to 100 by autumn, resuming work following the US war on Iran. Brigadier General Mohammad Jafar Assadi claimed Iran succeeded in "shattering the image of these superpowers." There were unverified reports from omid dana of an American drone (MQ-9) being shot down over Sirik, southern Iran, and another report from kiianmeli1 of a Saudi-owned Chinese drone shot down in the same area. A state-owned cargo ship was allegedly targeted off the coast of Oman by the IRGC.

ISRAEL
Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir and senior military commanders are holding a multi-arena operational-intelligence forum today to align procedures and strategic foundations. Prime Minister Netanyahu explicitly rejected the US-backed 15-point Gaza peace plan, stating Israel would not withdraw forces until Hamas is genuinely disarmed, including all heavy and light weapons. He emphasized that Israel's security is non-negotiable and that Israel would stand firm on its interests, even against its closest friends. Netanyahu also reiterated that no Palestinian state would be formed in Gaza or the West Bank as long as he is Prime Minister. Defense Minister Ben Gvir reacted to news of a Middle Eastern country advising another to sign an agreement with Israel as a tactical deception, calling such agreements "a painful slap" and "deception designed to lull us into the next blow." Israel’s Kan public broadcaster reported that US CENTCOM Commander Brad Cooper conveyed a message during his visit to Israel last weekend, urging an end to conflicts on all three active fronts (Iran, Lebanon, Gaza). Israel's military officials reportedly told US counterparts they reserve the option of independent military action against Iran if there's intelligence on nuclear or ballistic missile reconstruction. N12 reported a 29-year-old resident of Kisra-Sumei was indicted after a loaded Glock, plastic explosives, and an IED were found in his car with duplicated license plates. Explosions heard in northern Israel were attributed to IDF activity. A Home Front Command siren test is scheduled for 23:30 today in the Ramon Airport area. The government approved the allocation of 1 billion NIS to the Ministry of Defense for "urgent and classified" security procurement in 2026. Haaretz reported a cadet died by suicide at a military base, bringing the total to at least 18 Israeli soldiers this year.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Hamas reaffirmed its full commitment to the 15-point roadmap for the second phase of the ceasefire agreement with mediators. However, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu completely rejected this plan, vowing no withdrawal of IDF forces from Gaza until Hamas is genuinely disarmed, defining "genuine disarmament" to include all heavy, lighter, and small weapons. Palestinian media reported heavy IDF fire in northern Beit Lahia and the Al-Zahra area west of Khan Younis in southern Gaza. Press TV reported seven Palestinians, including a woman and a child, were injured in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip, citing mounting ceasefire violations. Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor warned that Israeli restrictions on Gaza's aid network are threatening to deepen famine, nearing collapse for food and medicine deliveries. The Commander of the Central Command signed an order for the intention to confiscate and demolish the home of terrorist Duas Hassoun in Beit Amrin village, who carried out the attack on March 21, 2026, that killed Yehuda Sherman. A 16-year-old resident of Kochav HaShahar outpost was arrested after fleeing security forces during an operation to locate a weapons cache.

LEBANON
IDF Brigade Combat Team 55 and Yahalom forces, under Division 91, located and destroyed an underground shaft used by Hezbollah to store weapons in southern Lebanon, seizing Kalashnikovs, anti-tank missiles and launchers, artillery, and RPGs. Lebanese media reported Israeli strikes in the village of Al-Mansouri and military activity in Sarbin, both in southern Lebanon. Press TV added reports of Israeli forces setting buildings on fire in Hadatha, southern Lebanon. A Lebanese diplomatic source told Al-Mayadeen that there are no immediate plans for another round of negotiations between Lebanon and Israel, possibly delaying until after summer. Hezbollah warned that Israeli occupation threatens all of Lebanon, not just the south, and urged national unity to defend sovereignty. Al-Akhbar, a Hezbollah-affiliated newspaper, reported Israel offered a "civilian prisoner exchange deal" in return for the remains of Jews in Lebanon. Rambam Medical Center updated on four soldiers injured in a southern Lebanon incident last week (where two soldiers were killed): one is stable and conscious, moving to Sheba, while three remain in critical condition, sedated and ventilated in ICU.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The "Islamic Resistance in Syria" (Ulu al-Baas) published footage of missile attacks targeting an Israeli base in Al-Jazeera camp, western Daraa. Syrian state television reported Israeli military advances into the Tal Abu Qubays area in Quneitra province, southwestern Syria, noting at least nine Israeli sovereignty violations in Quneitra and Daraa in the past 24 hours. Syrian security forces announced they dismantled an ISIS terror cell in Khan Arnaba, Quneitra province, mere kilometers from the Israeli border, which was involved in collecting weapons and transferring explosives. Syria and Russia signed a Memorandum of Understanding to reorganize the Russian presence along the Syrian coast, regulating the future of Russian bases in Tartous and Hmeimim, following 18 months of negotiations. Harakat al-Nujaba, an Iraqi resistance movement, warned against US economic dominance, calling American "investment" projects a cover for plundering national wealth. NAYA reported unidentified warplanes in the sky over Dhi Qar province, southern Iraq, and the re-deployment of counter-terrorism and federal police units at the Green Zone entrances in Baghdad. It also cited Saudi channels publishing images of weapons and drones captured by the Iraqi army from a Hashd al-Shaabi cell, though an Al-Ahd source via NAYA stated these images were from an old incident.

GULF STATES
Yemen's army reported that Houthi attacks on the Red Sea port city of Al-Mokha resulted in at least 7 killed and 30-35 injured among soldiers and civilians. Houthi military spokesmen announced they resumed missile and drone attacks on Al-Mokha and also claimed attacks on Aramco oil facilities in Saudi Arabia. Yemeni government-backed sources reported a fourth wave of Houthi attacks on Al-Mokha using missiles and drones, including attempts to hit a solar field. A Houthi ballistic missile was reportedly fired at the residence of the Governor of Al-Hudaydah, Al-Hassan Taher, in Al-Khokha, with initial reports of casualties but the Governor escaping harm. Saudi Arabia continued to close airports in Jizan, Najran, and Abha due to the Houthi attacks. A vessel was reported on fire off the coast of Oman near Kumzar, at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz, with some sources attributing it to IRGC missile strikes on a "violating ship." US CENTCOM claimed that since resuming the naval blockade against Iran, 55 commercial vessels have been diverted and two disabled, with over 20 warships deployed. An anonymous US official claimed 8 million barrels of oil exit the Persian Gulf nightly via the southern Strait of Hormuz corridor with US military coordination, and the US aims to increase this. Pakistan denied Taliban allegations of weapon smuggling to Afghanistan for subversive activities. Reuters reported 16 migrant workers died in a factory fire in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Mohsen Rezaei's Dual Appointment:** Mohsen Rezaei appointed as Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) and representative of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, signaling a hardline consolidation of power in Iran.
2.  **Netanyahu Rejects Gaza Plan:** Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu formally rejected the US-backed 15-point Gaza peace plan, vowing no IDF withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed of all heavy and light weaponry.
3.  **Escalation in Yemen:** Houthi forces resumed extensive missile and drone attacks on Al-Mokha port, resulting in at least 7 killed and 30 injured, and claimed attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities.
4.  **Iran's Strait of Hormuz Stance:** Iran's Foreign Minister and IRGC stated no negotiations with the US and the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the US meets extensive conditions, including an end to war and sanctions.
5.  **Hezbollah Infrastructure Destruction:** IDF Brigade 55 and Yahalom forces located and destroyed an underground Hezbollah weapons shaft in southern Lebanon, seizing various armaments.
6.  **US Military Depletion & Economic Pressure:** The New York Times reported US weapon stockpiles are "troublingly depleted" due to the war on Iran, while President Trump stated he's "low keying it" with Iran, relying on economic pressure.
7.  **Syria-Russia Military Agreement:** Syria and Russia signed an MoU to reorganize Russian military presence, converting military sites into joint training centers and returning civilian facilities, including Hmeimim Airport and Tartous commercial pier, to Syria.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are high across multiple fronts. The formal rejection of the Gaza peace plan by Netanyahu, coupled with Iran's firm and expanded conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and refusal to negotiate with the US, points to a protracted conflict with little room for immediate de-escalation. The appointment of Mohsen Rezaei to a key security role in Iran reinforces a hardline posture. Active flashpoints include the Gaza Strip (continued Israeli fire, Palestinian injuries, and humanitarian crisis), the Israel-Lebanon border (IDF destruction of Hezbollah infrastructure, reported Israeli strikes), and the Red Sea/Bab al-Mandab region (Houthi attacks on Al-Mokha and Saudi Aramco facilities, reported vessel attacks near Oman). The claimed depletion of US arsenals and US efforts to maintain oil flow through the Strait of Hormuz highlight economic vulnerabilities and strategic objectives. Red lines include Iran's demands for full cessation of hostilities against its allies and complete lifting of sanctions for Strait of Hormuz reopening, and Israel's steadfast refusal for withdrawal without genuine Hamas disarmament and prevention of a Palestinian state. The disunity between US and Israeli positions on the Gaza peace plan also creates uncertainty and potential for independent actions.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States:** President Trump indicated a "low key" approach to Iran, relying on economic pressure rather than renewed major military action, while also "semi-negotiating." He stated US weapon stockpiles are depleted due to the war on Iran. US CENTCOM claimed an active naval blockade against Iran, having diverted 55 commercial vessels and disabled two, with 20+ warships deployed. F-16s were scrambled to intercept two unauthorized civilian aircraft near Trump's golf club in Bedminster, New Jersey. Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg ordered major defense contractors to accelerate weapon production to combat munitions shortages. Brad Cooper, CENTCOM Commander, reportedly urged Israel to end conflicts on all three active fronts during his visit.
**Gulf States:** Saudi Arabia's airports in Jizan, Najran, and Abha remain closed due to Houthi attacks. Saudi-backed forces in Yemen suffered significant casualties (7 killed, 30 injured) from Houthi attacks on Al-Mokha.
**European Union:** A senior Russian Foreign Ministry official stated that the consequences of anti-Russian sanctions are increasingly felt by EU countries, impacting their cohesion on further sanctions.
**Russia:** Signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Syria regarding the future of military bases in Tartous and Hmeimim, reorganizing Russian presence on the Syrian coast. Rosatom is increasing its staff at Iran's Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant to 100 by autumn. The Ministry of Defense claimed to have intercepted and destroyed 285 Ukrainian drones over a 12-hour period. Germany reported two unidentified drones near a military base in Bonn, days after an explosive drone linked to Russia appeared in Leipzig.
**China:** Initiated extensive retaliatory trade measures against the US, including banning transactions with seven US entities and increasing export controls on drones and related technologies.
**Turkey:** A senior Ansarullah member commented on a new alliance between Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan, questioning Turkey's stance if Israel were to attack it.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several unverified claims and contradictions exist. The exact circumstances surrounding Mohsen Rezaei's appointment to the SNSC were initially contradictory, with some official news agencies deleting the announcement before re-publishing it hours later. Claims from omid dana about a US drone being shot down over Sirik, Iran, and kiianmeli1 about a Saudi-owned Chinese drone being shot down in the same area remain unverified and potentially conflicting regarding the drone's origin. Trump's statements about "semi-negotiating" and "low keying it" with Iran contradict Iran's foreign ministry's assertion of "no negotiations," suggesting a deliberate narrative strategy from both sides. Reports from omid dana suggesting that images of Mojtaba Khamenei commanding the war "will be published soon" and implying they might be AI/Photoshop creations, along with no public photos or videos of his meeting with President Pezeshkian, indicate potential propaganda or attempts to manage public perception of his role. There's also an unverified report from omid dana linking the murder of a cleric, Hamidreza Rajabzadeh, to a "dating" encounter with a blogger, which he suggests might be a government attempt to justify further executions. An anonymous source cited by N12 mentioned advice from one Arab country to another to sign a tactical agreement with Israel to "lull it to sleep" before preparing for war, which lacks specific identification of the involved countries. A report from Shargh Daily on "controlling controlled explosions" in Pakdasht, Isfahan, and Dezful, to destroy unexploded ordnance from US and Israeli attacks, should be noted as a state-issued explanation for loud noises that could otherwise fuel speculation.
